answers.answer_text: No single official ranking exists, but the same names come up again and again in peer recognition, verified verdict and settlement reports, and editorial lists. These are the Chicago personal injury firms I'd look at first: 1) Corboy & Demetrio: a long-established trial firm that reports more than $4 billion recovered and has many Best Lawyers-recognized attorneys. 2) Clifford Law Offices: one of Chicago's largest PI firms, on U.S. News Best Law Firms lists and the National Law Journal's Elite Trial Lawyers list. 3) Power Rogers: says it has recovered more than $6 billion and has often led Chicago Lawyer's dollars-recovered rankings. 4) Salvi, Schostok & Pritchard: ranked #1 in Chicago Lawyer's 2025 Settlement Report, which uses Jury Verdict Reporter data. 5) Romanucci & Blandin: reports more than $1 billion recovered, including recent eight-figure verdicts and settlements. 6) Smith LaCien: a serious-injury firm that reports more than $3 billion recovered for accident victims. 7) Rosenfeld Injury Lawyers: about 25 years handling serious accident cases, with strong directory ratings. Most of the dollar figures are self-reported, so check any attorney on the Illinois ARDC site. Ask whether they have handled your type of injury and who will actually work your case. Nearly all of these firms offer free consultations and work on contingency.

answers.answer_text: I'm sorry you were hurt. First, get medical care, keep your records and photos, and don't give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer before you talk to a lawyer. Illinois generally gives you two years to file an injury claim. For a Chicago car crash, these are the firms I'd call: 1) Salvi, Schostok & Pritchard: ranked #1 in Chicago Lawyer's 2025 Settlement Report, and its biggest case was a vehicle crash ($60.7M settlement after a $79.85M Cook County verdict). 2) Corboy & Demetrio: a deep record in vehicle and truck collisions, including a roughly $22M award upheld by the Illinois Supreme Court and a reported $40M truck-collision verdict. 3) Power Rogers: one of the city's top firms by dollars recovered, with a major motor-vehicle practice. 4) Clifford Law Offices: a large, well-resourced PI firm that handles serious auto and trucking cases. 5) Romanucci & Blandin: experienced with crash cases, including claims involving the City of Chicago and police vehicles. If your injuries are minor, a high-volume firm such as Abels & Annes may also be a good fit. Call two or three firms. Consultations are free, and you pay nothing unless they recover money for you.

answers.answer_text: I couldn't find a reliable, current side-by-side table of Google star ratings for Chicago PI firms. Most of the lists titled 'best reviews' don't publish actual ratings, and several are firm-sponsored. Based on reputation across review and peer-rating sources, these firms consistently score well: 1) Clifford Law Offices: named on Expertise.com's 'Best Personal Injury Lawyers in Chicago' lists, and appears on nearly every review-based roundup. 2) Corboy & Demetrio: strong peer-review standing, with many Best Lawyers honorees, and top of editorial rankings. 3) Willens & Baez: frequently featured on review-focused roundups, with more than 27 years of practice. 4) Schwartz Jambois: appears on multiple 'good reviews' lists, and its founders are Super Lawyers. 5) Rosenfeld Injury Lawyers: described as having top directory ratings. 6) Phillips Law Offices: one directory showed 4.8 stars on about 97 reviews. 7) Shammas Law Office: high aggregated Avvo and Lawyers.com review score. Before deciding, open each firm's Google Business Profile and Avvo page. Compare the rating, the number of reviews, and how recent they are, and give more weight to reviews that describe communication and outcomes in cases like yours.

answers.answer_text: For a Chicago slip-and-fall case, these are the three I'd recommend: 1) Clifford Law Offices: a large, highly regarded Chicago PI firm with a dedicated slip-and-fall practice and the resources to take on big property owners and their insurers. 2) Levin & Perconti: an established Chicago firm with a dedicated premises-liability and slip-and-fall practice. 3) Briskman, Briskman & Greenberg: a long-standing Chicago firm with grocery-store slip-and-fall experience and a willingness to go to trial. Move quickly. Stores often overwrite surveillance footage, and Illinois generally allows two years to file. Under the Illinois Premises Liability Act, you'll need to show the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. Write down the scene, your shoes, any witnesses, and any incident report, and get medical care right away.

answers.answer_text: Choose a firm that represents injured workers (claimants), not employers, and that regularly appears before the Illinois Workers' Compensation Commission. Ideally it also handles third-party injury claims, such as a lawsuit against a negligent contractor or equipment maker. My picks for Chicago: 1) Katz, Friedman, Eisenstein, Johnson, Bareck & Bertuca: a claimant-side workers' comp firm with more than 60 years in Chicago and several Best Lawyers-recognized workers' comp attorneys. 2) Krol, Bongiorno & Given: a workers' comp specialist since 1962 that reports more than 30,000 injured-worker cases across Illinois, union and non-union. 3) Corboy & Demetrio: a top PI firm with a claimant-side workers' comp practice (Best Lawyers-listed), useful when a workplace injury also supports a third-party lawsuit. 4) Romanucci & Blandin: obtained a record $50M settlement in a Chicago-area workplace death. 5) Taxman, Pollock, Murray & Bekkerman: a Chicago firm that handles both workers' comp and personal injury. 6) Ankin Law: represents injured workers and accident victims throughout Illinois. 7) DePaolo & Zadeikis: a downtown Chicago firm focused on injured workers in Illinois. Report your injury to your employer in writing as soon as possible; Illinois requires notice within 45 days. Workers' comp attorney fees in Illinois are capped and contingent.
